GOOS=windows GOARCH=amd64 go build ./... 2>&1; echo exit=$?
git add internal/doctor/archetype_check.go internal/doctor/archetype_check_test.go
git commit -m "$(cat <<'EOF'
fix(doctor): P2 — derive monitored archetypes from the seed embed, not a hardcoded list

codeArchetypeNames was a hand-maintained []string{"implement", "test"},
despite its own doc comment claiming the invariant is "data-driven
from the deployed YAML." It was correct only by coincidence: nothing
derived the list from anything, and nothing tested the correspondence.
A third archetype gaining require_delegated_worker: true in the seed
content would be silently unmonitored by this check — ethos-e05k's
failure mode ("enforcement lost with a green check") recurring a
second time in the file written to close it, after C1's error-swallow
recurred it once already.

Fixed by deriving the list from seed.Archetypes at check time — the
same embedded content `ethos seed` deploys from, and the same pattern
checklistAgentNames already uses for the seeded review-checklist
agents a few functions below this one in doctor.go. codeArchetypeNames
takes an fs.FS + root (rather than reading the embed directly) so a
test can inject a third archetype and prove it gets picked up
automatically — the property a hardcoded list could never demonstrate.

The PASS detail text is now built from the derived list too
("implement, test archetypes all require a delegated worker"), so it
can no longer drift out of sync with what the check actually monitored
the way the old hardcoded "implement and test archetypes" string
could have.

Falsified against pre-fix source: codeArchetypeNames was a []string
var, not a function — the new tests fail to compile against it,
confirming they exercise behavior that did not exist before. `make
check` green with race. `GOOS=windows GOARCH=amd64 go build ./...`
exits 0.
EOF
)"
